s: Pivot the events: one MAX(CASE WHEN Event = 'Shipped' THEN EventTimeUTC END) per milestone, grouped by OrderID.
Lags in hours from the timestamps (JULIANDAY in SQLite, DATEDIFF in SQL Server).
Delivered-within-5-days as a 0/1 flag so it can be averaged.
In a warehouse, MERGE the snapshot nightly: new orders insert, existing ones update the milestones they reached.

code.title: Fulfilment snapshot (SQLite date functions; see the note for SQL Server)
src: MAX(CASE WHEN Event = 'Placed'    THEN EventTimeUTC END) AS PlacedAt,
MAX(CASE WHEN Event = 'Picked'    THEN EventTimeUTC END) AS PickedAt,
MAX(CASE WHEN Event = 'Shipped'   THEN EventTimeUTC END) AS ShippedAt,
MAX(CASE WHEN Event = 'Delivered' THEN EventTimeUTC END) AS DeliveredAt
SUM(CASE WHEN DeliveredAt IS NOT NULL AND (JULIANDAY(DeliveredAt) - JULIANDAY(PlacedAt)) * 24 <= 120 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DeliveredWithin5Days

s: Find the last snapshot date per month, then sum stock for that date only.
The naive SUM adds every weekly snapshot: wrong for any period longer than one snapshot.
Additive across products and warehouses; semi-additive over time (last value, or average for "average stock").

s: Tickets have a lifecycle with milestones (opened, assigned, resolved): accumulating snapshot, one row per ticket, lags as measures.
Balances are levels at a point in time: periodic snapshot, customer × month, semi-additive.
Promotion coverage must record products that didn't sell: factless fact at product × store × promotion × day.
Page views are events: transaction fact at one row per view (high volume; aggregate tables for reporting).
